fieldMarks: Males about 73 kg with a thick neck and shoulder ruff; females about 36 kg
Curved horns: males to 450 mm, females to 190 mm
Winter coat darker, summer coat lighter brown
Young uniformly brown with black front legs
behavior: Herds of 2-23; males separate from females outside the breeding season
Most active at dawn and dusk; moves up and down slopes daily
Grazes alpine herbs and subalpine plants
habitat: Rugged, mostly wooded slopes and rocky ground at 750-5,000 m.
range: Native to the Himalaya from Kashmir through northern India to Nepal and Sikkim, and southern Tibet. Introduced in New Zealand, California and South Africa (NatureServe); Animal Diversity Web also lists New Mexico and Ontario.
